messages:
lucy: quick follow-up from the fragmentation triage this morning — short thread with results, configs, and next steps.

omar: pls summarize the failure mode we saw in prod.

lucy: summary: shared model cache on multi-tenant nodes produced many small NVMe demotes when multiple tenants accessed disjoint weight ranges that lived within the same allocator chunk. The spill pattern was ~2000 small writes/min vs baseline ~400. CPU diff negligible, but p95 latency for small-batch chat rose ~11ms during spikes.

feng: was the allocator coalescing across tenants? we should never combine pages across tenant boundaries.

lucy: turned out it did for shared caches — we allowed coalescing when allow_shared flag was true. chunk headers lacked owner granularity so demote created large scattered IO.

zara: can you paste the probe config you ran in prod canary?

lucy: yes — toggles on runtime image for canary run:

```
--cache.mode=shared
--allocator.chunk_size=131072  # 128KB
--allocator.allow_shared_coalesce=true
--evict.batch_ms=50
--telemetry.compactness_window=300000
```

lucy: we then ran the canary with shared=true (24h) and an A/B with shared=false. shared=false reduced small NVMe writes by ~78% and eliminated the p95 tail regressions.

omar: interesting. did metadata overhead change? we previously discussed owner bits per slot.

feng: for the fix we prototyped a per-slot owner tag (1 byte) plus a 2-byte chunk-compactness field. measured overhead ~2.1% host memory at 32KB slot size. tradeoff seems acceptable given NVMe savings.

zara: concurrency: how do we update owner tags under compaction without races?

feng: we used an epoch-based update: compaction increments epoch, writes tombstones, flips owner bits, then publishes epoch. evict path reads epoch and if mismatch falls back to single-page demote. cheap on common path.

lucy: added instrumentation: per-tenant small_write_rate, chunk_owner_conflict_rate, and compactness_ratio. alerted when small_write_rate > 1000/min per node.

omar: what's the behavioral change we want? disallow shared coalescing by default and make it opt-in for tenants that explicitly opt-in via hint API?

lucy: proposal: default runtime config = tenant-isolated coalesce. Add a residency-hint API for shared caches: {slot_index, desired_shared_group, allow_shared:bool, priority_hint}. compiler/cacher can emit shared-group hints.

zara: sample proto?

lucy: inline sketch:

```
message CacheHint {
  uint64 slot_index = 1;
  optional string shared_group = 2;
  bool allow_shared = 3;
  enum Priority { LOW=0; NORMAL=1; HIGH=2; }
  Priority priority = 4;
}
```

lucy: ops question: tenant flip safety — if a tenant opts into shared-group, how do we roll that out without causing oscillation?

feng: require central config service confirmation + per-tenant cooldown (10m) and 2 successive windows of compactness checks before enabling. Also leadership lease prevents cross-node rapid toggles.

omar: rollback plan if we see regressions in prod?

lucy: immediate per-tenant kill-switch to disable allow_shared for that tenant; global kill-switch on config service to revert default to isolated coalesce. nodes treat kill-switch as high-priority config and apply within 60s.

zara: ops wants a playbook entry: how to identify shared-coalesce regressions (queries to run).

lucy: added to playbook: 1) check chunk_owner_conflict_rate > 0.1% and small_write_rate spike, 2) examine recent demote write sizes (if median < 64KB and counts high), 3) run quick A/B by toggling allow_shared on a single node. I've added CLI examples in the playbook.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of cache-fix:v1 started on canary cluster ci-27 — 2026-03-23T18:12:44Z

feng: one more thought: compress the owner tags for long runs to reduce overhead. we can delta-encode owner ids across adjacent slots.

lucy: agreed — add compression as follow-up (non-blocking). Priority is to stop the small-write storm.

omar: schedule: 1) revert default to isolated coalesce, 2) ship per-slot owner tag + epoch semantics, 3) add telemetry + playbook, 4) RFC appendix for hint API. target 1-week canary then 2-week ramp.

zara: thanks. ping @ops-bot to prepare runbook and pageplay. :white_check_mark:
